## Kriging for soil pH across ontario districts

```{r}
variogram = variogram(value_avg~1, soil_ontario) 
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Variogram of soil measurements(phH values) in Indiana. The number beside the points indicates the number of points from the variogram cloud that were in that particular bin."}
variogram |>
  plot(plot.numbers =TRUE,
       ylab =expression(gamma(h)),
       xlab = "Distance (h) in metres",
       pch =16)
```

```{r}
# different variogram models 
variogram_spherical  = fit.variogram(variogram, vgm(1, "Sph", 50000, 1))
variogram_gaussian = fit.variogram(variogram, vgm(1, "Gau", 40000, 1))
variogram_exponential = fit.variogram(variogram, vgm(1, "Exp", 50000, 1))
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Visualizing different variogram models"}
#plot the various models
plot(gamma~dist, variogram,
     ylab =expression(gamma(h)),
     xlab = "Distance (h) in metres",
     pch =16)
lines(variogramLine(variogram_exponential, 1.075 * max(variogram$dist)), 
      lty = 1, col = 'purple', lwd = 2)
lines(variogramLine(variogram_spherical, 1.075 * max(variogram$dist)), 
      lty = 1, col = 'orange', lwd = 2)
lines(variogramLine(variogram_gaussian, 1.075 * max(variogram$dist)), 
      lty = 1, col = 'green', lwd = 2)
legend(x = "bottomright", legend = c("Exponential","Spherical","Gaussian"), 
       col = c("purple","orange","green"), 
       lty = c(1,1,1),
       lwd = c(2,2,2))
```

```{r, echo =FALSE, fig.cap = "Anisotropic sample variograms"}
# Anisotropic variogram models
variogram_anis = variogram(value_avg~1, soil_ontario, alpha = c(0,45,90,135))

variogram_anis |> ggplot(aes(x= dist, y=gamma))+
  geom_point()+
  facet_grid(.~dir.hor)

```


```{r}
# block kriging to identify ideal pH
block_krige <- krige(value_avg~1, soil_ontario,
                     ontario_district, variogram_gaussian, block = c(10000, 10000))
```

```{r}
#block kriging for counties with ideal pH suitable for agriculture
block_krige$suitable <- ifelse(block_krige$var1.pred >= 6.0 &
                        block_krige$var1.pred <= 7.5,
                        "Suitable", "Not Suitable")

```



```{r, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Comparing block-kriged averages (left-blues) to block-kriged averages (right-greens). Note that the green block-kriged values tend to define suitability better."}



# Plot 1: pH Range
gg1 <- ggplot(block_krige) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = var1.pred), color = "white") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "pH Range") +  # or use scale_fill_distiller()
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "right") +
  ggtitle("Block-Kriged pH Range")

# Plot 2: Suitability
gg2 <- ggplot(block_krige) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = suitable), color = "white") +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("lightgreen", "darkgreen"),
    name = "pH Suitability"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "right") +
  ggtitle("Districts with Suitable Soil pH")

# Arrange side-by-side
gg1 + gg2  # using patchwork


```

## Formating crop data for modeling

```{r}


# 1. Add lon/lat to original sf object
crop_hist_sf <- crop_hist_sf %>%
  mutate(
    lon = st_coordinates(geometry)[, 1],
    lat = st_coordinates(geometry)[, 2]
  )

# 2. Pivot both yield and area to long format
yield_long <- crop_hist_sf %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("y"),
    names_to = "year",
    names_prefix = "y",
    values_to = "yield"
  )

area_long <- crop_hist_sf %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("a"),
    names_to = "year",
    names_prefix = "a",
    values_to = "area"
  )

# 3. Join them back together
crop_long <- left_join(yield_long, area_long,
                       by = c("caruid", "crop", "year", "lon", "lat"))

# 4. Final touch: convert year to numeric
crop_long <- crop_long %>%
  mutate(year = as.integer(year)) %>%
dplyr::select(year, caruid, crop, yield, area, lon, lat) |>
dplyr:: filter(yield != -999, area != -999)|>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = crs)




```

build the INLA model

```{r}
formula <- yield ~ 
  f(ogf_id, model = "bym", graph = "ontario.graph") +
  f(year, model = "rw1") +
  f(crop, model = "iid") +
  area

result <- inla(
  formula, 
  family = "gaussian",  # or "gamma" if yield is skewed
  data = crop_ontario,
  control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE),
  control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE)
)

```

Getting the average slope for the areas

```{r}
krige_variable <- function(var_name, new_col_name, grid_sp) {
  # 1. Prep soil points
  soil_var <- soil_clean %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[var_name]])) %>%
    st_transform(st_crs(corn_data_sf)) %>%
    st_centroid(of_largest_polygon = TRUE)

  soil_sp <- as(soil_var, "Spatial")

  # 2. Variogram + model
  v <- variogram(as.formula(paste0(var_name, " ~ 1")), data = soil_sp)
  model <- fit.variogram(v, model = vgm(1, "Exp", 100000, 0.1))

  # 3. Kriging
  kriged <- krige(
    as.formula(paste0(var_name, " ~ 1")),
    soil_sp,
    newdata = grid_sp,
    model = model,
    nmax = 30
  )

  kriged_sf <- st_as_sf(kriged) %>%
    st_set_crs(st_crs(corn_data_sf))

  # 4. Spatial join to crop regions
  joined <- st_join(kriged_sf, corn_data_sf, join = st_within, left = FALSE)

  # 5. Average by region
  summary <- joined %>%
    st_drop_geometry() %>%
    group_by(county, year) %>%
    summarise(!!new_col_name := mean(var1.pred, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

  return(summary)
}

```

  left_join(slope_summary, by = c("county", "year")) %>%
  left_join(kfactor_summary, by = c("county", "year")) %>%
  distinct(county, year, .keep_all = TRUE)  # clean duplicates

#will figure this out later
#grouping the soil textures into more general categories
soil_clean <- soil_clean %>%
  mutate(
    texture_group = case_when(
      atexture1 %in% c("CL", "SCL", "SICL") ~ "Clay Loam",
      atexture1 %in% c("SL", "FSL", "GSL", "GL", "GLS", "VFSL", "LVFS") ~ "Sandy Loam",
      atexture1 %in% c("L", "SIL", "VAR") ~ "Loam",
      atexture1 %in% c("C", "SIC") ~ "Clay",
      atexture1 %in% c("S", "FS", "VFS", "LS", "LFS", "CSL", "LCS") ~ "Sand",
      atexture1 %in% c("ORG") ~ "Organic",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    )
  )

soil_clean <- soil_clean %>%
  mutate(drainage_group = case_when(
    drainage1 %in% c("W", "WA") ~ "Well Drained",
    drainage1 %in% c("MW") ~ "Moderately Well",
    drainage1 %in% c("P", "VP") ~ "Poorly Drained",
    drainage1 %in% c("VR", "VA", "R") ~ "Very Poor",
    drainage1 %in% c("I") ~ "Imperfect",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  ))

soil_cats <- soil_clean %>%
  filter(!is.na(texture_group) & !is.na(drainage_group)) %>%
  st_transform(st_crs(corn_data_sf)) %>%
  st_join(corn_data_sf, join = st_within, left = FALSE)

# Texture mode
texture_summary <- soil_cats %>%
  group_by(county, year) %>%
  summarise(texture_mode = names(sort(table(texture_group), decreasing = TRUE)[1]), .groups = "drop")

# Drainage mode
drainage_summary <- soil_cats %>%
  group_by(county, year) %>%
  summarise(drainage_mode = names(sort(table(drainage_group), decreasing = TRUE)[1]), .groups = "drop")

corn_data_sf <- corn_data_sf %>%
  left_join(texture_summary, by = c("county", "year")) %>%
  left_join(drainage_summary, by = c("county", "year")) %>%
  distinct(county, year, .keep_all = TRUE)

#plot to check
corn_texture <- ggplot(corn_data_sf %>% filter(year == 2004)) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = texture_mode), color = "grey40") +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(name = "Texture") +
  labs(title = "Most Common Soil Texture by Region (2004)") +
  theme_minimal()

corn_drain <- ggplot(corn_data_sf %>% filter(year == 2004)) +

  scale_fill_viridis_d(name = "Texture") +

## Corn Yield

The corn growing season is from May-October.  
```{r}
#weather during the corn growing season for each year/station
weather_corn_gs <- weather %>%
  filter(month %in% 5:10)

head(weather_corn_gs)
colSums(is.na(weather_corn_gs))
```
```{r}
# Step 1: Identify rows with missing total_precip
weather_na <- weather_corn_gs %>% filter(is.na(total_precip))

# Step 2: Identify complete rows (non-NA total_precip)
weather_complete <- weather_corn_gs %>% filter(!is.na(total_precip))

# Step 3: Find nearest neighbor for each NA entry
nearest_idx <- st_nearest_feature(weather_na, weather_complete)

# Step 4: Fill NA values from nearest station's total_precip
weather_corn_gs$total_precip[is.na(weather_corn_gs$total_precip)] <- 
  weather_complete$total_precip[nearest_idx]

sum(is.na(weather_corn_gs$total_precip))

```

#### 2024 Forecast

```{r, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE}

#attaching a station's information to the yield
corn_regions <- dplyr::select(corn_data_sf, county, geom)

weather_with_county <- st_join(weather_corn_gs, corn_regions, join = st_nearest_feature)


# Step 1: Fill in all county-year-month combinations (May–October)
weather_avg_complete <- weather_with_county %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  group_by(county, year, month) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_temp = mean(mean_temp, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_precip = mean(total_precip, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_humidity = mean(max_humidity, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  complete(county, year, month = 5:10)  # Ensures full seasonal structure

# Step 2: Fill in missing weather values within each county and month
weather_avg_filled <- weather_avg_complete %>%
  group_by(county, month) %>%
  fill(mean_temp, total_precip, max_humidity, .direction = "downup") %>%
  ungroup()

# Step 3: Reshape to wide format (one row per county-year)
weather_wide <- weather_avg_filled %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = month,
    values_from = c(mean_temp, total_precip, max_humidity),
    names_glue = "{.value}_m{month}"
  )

```

#### Autoregression 
```{r}
#creating a lag to to capture the patterns from the previous time step
full_corn_data <- full_corn_data %>%
  arrange(county, year) %>%
  group_by(county) %>%
  mutate(yield_lag1 = dplyr::lag(yield, n = 1)) %>%
  ungroup()
```

```{r}
#training and test sets for the ar
corn_train <- full_corn_data %>% filter(year < 2024)
corn_test <- full_corn_data %>% filter(year == 2024)
```

```{r}
# Identify counties with missing weather for 2024
missing_weather_2024 <- full_corn_data %>%
  filter(year == 2024 & (is.na(mean_temp_m5) | is.na(total_precip_m5))) %>%
  dplyr::select(county)

# Create sf objects for missing and available counties
missing_sf <- corn_data_sf %>%
  filter(year == 2024, county %in% missing_weather_2024$county)

available_sf <- corn_data_sf %>%
  filter(year == 2024, !county %in% missing_weather_2024$county)

# Get available weather variables
available_weather <- full_corn_data %>%
  filter(year == 2024, !county %in% missing_weather_2024$county) %>%
  dplyr::select(county, starts_with("mean_temp"), starts_with("total_precip"))

# Find nearest available county
nearest_idx <- sf::st_nearest_feature(missing_sf, available_sf)

# Get matched weather
imputed_weather <- available_weather[nearest_idx, ] %>%
  dplyr::select(starts_with("mean_temp"), starts_with("total_precip"))

# Rebuild missing counties with imputed weather
missing_filled <- full_corn_data %>%
  filter(year == 2024 & county %in% missing_weather_2024$county) %>%
  dplyr::select(-starts_with("mean_temp"), -starts_with("total_precip")) %>%
  bind_cols(imputed_weather)

# Keep only non-NA rows
full_corn_data <- full_corn_data %>%
  filter(!(year == 2024 & county %in% missing_weather_2024$county))

# Add back imputed rows
full_corn_data <- bind_rows(full_corn_data, missing_filled)
```

```{r}
corn_model_ar1_full <- lm(
  yield ~ yield_lag1 +
    mean_temp_m5 + mean_temp_m6 + mean_temp_m7 + mean_temp_m8 + mean_temp_m9 + mean_temp_m10 +
    total_precip_m5 + total_precip_m6 + total_precip_m7 + total_precip_m8 + total_precip_m9 + total_precip_m10 +
    slope1_avg + kfactor_avg,
  data = corn_train
)
```

```{r}
corn_test$yield_pred_ar1 <- predict(corn_model_ar1_full, newdata = corn_test)

corn_test %>%
  filter(is.na(full_corn_data)) %>%
  dplyr::select(county, year, yield_lag1, mean_temp_m5, total_precip_m5)
```

#### Random Walk 1

```{r}
# Random Walk 1: Predict 2024 yield as the 2023 yield (lag1)
full_corn_data <- full_corn_data %>%
  arrange(county, year) %>%
  group_by(county) %>%
  mutate(yield_rw1 = lag(yield, n = 1)) %>%
  ungroup()

corn_rw1_2024 <- full_corn_data %>%
  filter(year == 2024, !is.na(yield_rw1)) %>%
  mutate(yield_pred_rw1 = yield_rw1)
```

#### Random Walk 2
```{r}
full_corn_data <- full_corn_data %>%
  arrange(county, year) %>%
  group_by(county) %>%
  mutate(yield_rw2 = 2 * lag(yield, 1) - lag(yield, 2)) %>%
  ungroup()


corn_rw2_2024 <- full_corn_data %>%
  filter(year == 2024, !is.na(yield_rw2)) %>%
  mutate(yield_pred_rw2 = yield_rw2)
```

#### Model Evaluations

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(Metrics)

# Combine actuals and predictions
corn_2024_predictions <- corn_data_sf %>%
  filter(year == 2024) %>%
  dplyr::select(County = county, Actual_Yield_2024 = yield_bushels_ac) %>%
  mutate(Actual_Yield_2024 = as.numeric(Actual_Yield_2024)) %>%
  left_join(dplyr::select(corn_test, County = county, Pred_AR1 = yield_pred_ar1), by = "County") %>%
  left_join(dplyr::select(corn_rw1_2024, County = county, Pred_RW1 = yield_pred_rw1), by = "County") %>%
  left_join(dplyr::select(corn_rw2_2024, County = county, Pred_RW2 = yield_pred_rw2), by = "County") %>%
  mutate(
    Resid_AR1 = Pred_AR1 - Actual_Yield_2024,
    Resid_RW1 = Pred_RW1 - Actual_Yield_2024,
    Resid_RW2 = Pred_RW2 - Actual_Yield_2024
  )

# Compute overall RMSE for each model
rmse_ar1 <- rmse(corn_2024_predictions$Actual_Yield_2024, corn_2024_predictions$Pred_AR1)
rmse_rw1 <- rmse(corn_2024_predictions$Actual_Yield_2024, corn_2024_predictions$Pred_RW1)
rmse_rw2 <- rmse(corn_2024_predictions$Actual_Yield_2024, corn_2024_predictions$Pred_RW2)

# Create final RMSE row
rmse_row <- tibble(
  County = "Overall RMSE",
  Actual_Yield_2024 = NA,
  Pred_AR1 = NA,
  Pred_RW1 = NA,
  Pred_RW2 = NA,
  Resid_AR1 = rmse_ar1,
  Resid_RW1 = rmse_rw1,
  Resid_RW2 = rmse_rw2
)

# Bind to table
final_table <- bind_rows(corn_2024_predictions, rmse_row)

# View
print(final_table)


```
```{r}
total_comparison <- corn_2024_predictions %>%

    Total_Actual = sum(Actual_Yield_2024, na.rm = TRUE),

    Total_Pred_RW1 = sum(Pred_RW1, na.rm = TRUE),
    Total_Pred_RW2 = sum(Pred_RW2, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%

    Error_AR1 = abs(Total_Pred_AR1 - Total_Actual),

    Mean_Pred_RW2 = mean(Pred_RW2, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%

  )

#### 2025 Forecast

The autoregression performed the best, so using that.

Making a data set for 2025
```{r}
# Get historical averages for Aug–Oct by county
hist_avg_late <- weather_avg %>%
  filter(month %in% 8:10) %>%
  group_by(county, month) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_temp = mean(mean_temp, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_precip = mean(total_precip, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_humidity = mean(max_humidity, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Merge with 2025 actual data up to July and fill missing with averages
weather_2025_filled <- weather_avg %>%
  filter(year == 2025) %>%
  full_join(hist_avg_late, by = c("county", "month")) %>%
  mutate(
    mean_temp = ifelse(is.na(mean_temp.x), mean_temp.y, mean_temp.x),
    total_precip = ifelse(is.na(total_precip.x), total_precip.y, total_precip.x),
    max_humidity = ifelse(is.na(max_humidity.x), max_humidity.y, max_humidity.x)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(county, month, mean_temp, total_precip, max_humidity, year = year) %>%
  replace_na(list(year = 2025))

weather_2025_wide <- weather_2025_filled %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = month,
    values_from = c(mean_temp, total_precip, max_humidity),
    names_glue = "{.value}_m{month}"
  )

```

```{r}
corn_2024_yield <- full_corn_data %>%
  filter(year == 2024) %>%
  dplyr::select(county, yield_lag1 = yield)

corn_2025 <- corn_2024_yield %>%
  left_join(weather_2025_wide, by = "county") %>%
  left_join(
    full_corn_data %>%
      filter(year == 2024) %>%
      dplyr::select(county, slope1_avg, kfactor_avg) %>%
      distinct(),
    by = "county"
  ) %>%
  mutate(year = 2025)

```
